skill.summary: Set up k-skill installation, CLI access, credential handling, and optional update checks with approval before external changes.
skill.author: nomadamas

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are benign documentation, restricted credential-file setup, or metadata checks; no evidence found of credential exfiltration or concealed malware. Global updates and scheduled execution of mutable npm packages retain genuine supply-chain and persistence risks despite consent requirements. Separately, the adapter promotes remotely fetched CLI output to primary instructions without binding it to the reviewed source.

remediation.issue: The adapter executes a mutable major-version CLI and treats its output as primary instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited CLI release and verify package integrity. Bundle the reviewed instructions and treat retrieved text as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: The default update operation can replace global skills across multiple coding agents.
remediation.suggestion: Default to check-only behavior. Show affected agents, skills, and versions, then obtain explicit approval before each update.

remediation.issue: Optional cron and Windows tasks repeatedly execute an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Use an integrity-verified local checker. Make task creation idempotent, avoid silently replacing existing tasks, and document removal commands.

content.user_title: Configure the k-skill Bundle and Runtime
content.value_statement: Setting up k-skill requires coordinating installation, CLI access, and credential handling. This skill guides those steps and offers optional update checks with approval requirements.
actual_capabilities: Guide bundle installation through the skills CLI or Claude Code marketplace plugins.
Retrieve skill instructions, file listings, and bundled helpers through the unified k-skill CLI.
Explain credential resolution through environment variables, agent vaults, and an optional fallback file.
Check fallback-file existence and owner-only permissions with the bundled Bash helper.
Provide consent-gated cron and Windows Task Scheduler examples for periodic update checks.
Offer an optional GitHub repository star through an authenticated GitHub CLI after approval.
limitations: The documented CLI workflow requires Node.js 18 or later and npm package access.
The bundled helper checks only file existence and mode 0600, not credential validity, service connectivity, or runtime availability.
The external CLI implementation and hosted proxy services are not included in the reviewed files.
The Bash verifier is not Windows-native; the Windows scheduling example requires platform-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Development Workstation
use_cases.description: Choose one bundle installation method, confirm CLI access, and identify only the credentials required by selected skills.
use_cases.target_user: Developers using Claude Code or Codex

use_cases.title: Configure Vault-Based Credentials
use_cases.description: Check Dolshoi vault prerequisites and request missing credentials without asking users to paste secret values into chat.

use_cases.title: Plan Periodic Update Checks
use_cases.description: Review the optional scheduler examples, assess package execution risks, and approve only the required check task.
use_cases.target_user: Workstation maintainers responsible for agent skill updates

prompt_templates.title: Review Setup Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the k-skill setup requirements for my workstation. Identify prerequisites and existing installations without installing packages, updating skills, or creating files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the setup before authorizing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Installation Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the skills CLI and Claude Code plugin installation paths for my environment. Show proposed changes and request approval before executing either path.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: select one installation route and avoid duplicate installs.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Credentials and Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Determine whether my selected skills need credentials and whether a vault is available. Report variable names and verification limits without displaying secret values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: configure credential handling without unnecessary fallback files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Scheduled Check Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the update-check example for my operating system. Identify mutable-package execution, existing task conflicts, and removal steps before proposing any scheduled task.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: assess persistent update checks before authorizing scheduler changes.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: assess a vault-enabled workstation without making changes.
output: Installation: an existing skills CLI installation is available; no duplicate plugin installation is proposed.
Credentials: use the available vault; do not create a plaintext fallback file.
Next step: approve a reviewed CLI release before running verification.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: explain a fallback-file check when the file exists with mode 0644.
output: Result: the fallback file has broader permissions than the helper permits.
Expected permissions: 0600, allowing only the owner to read and write.
Scope: this check does not establish credential validity or service availability.
Next step: confirm the fallback file is necessary, then approve permission correction.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: review the optional daily update check before scheduling it.
output: Schedule: the documented example checks daily at 09:00.
Security concern: the helper invokes an unpinned npm package on each run.
Decision: defer task creation until the checker version and removal procedure are reviewed.

best_practices: Review and pin the CLI package before execution, and request explicit approval for installation, global updates, scheduling, and GitHub changes.
Use a vault when available, prepare only required credentials, and never paste secret values into chat.
Distinguish file-permission checks from runtime and service validation; document approved scheduled tasks and their removal procedures.
anti_patterns: Running the default update as a harmless check even though it can replace global skills across coding agents.
Creating credential files for proxy-backed skills that do not require user secrets.
Adding recurring tasks or unrelated automation without explicit approval and review of the executed package.

faq.question: Which agent tools does this setup target?
faq.answer: The instructions describe general skills CLI installation for coding agents and a separate Claude Code plugin route. Claude, Codex, and Claude Code are listed.

faq.question: Do I need to install the CLI globally?
faq.answer: No. The documented default uses npx. Global installation is optional for users who need a persistent command.

faq.question: Must I create a secrets.env file?
faq.answer: No. Prefer environment variables or a vault. Many proxy-backed features need no user API key, and Dolshoi mode prohibits creating this file.

faq.question: What does the bundled verification script check?
faq.answer: It checks whether the selected secrets file exists and has mode 0600. It does not validate secret values, Node.js, or remote services.

faq.question: Does update only check for new versions?
faq.answer: No. The default update can refresh the CLI and global agent skills. The instructions provide check-only alternatives and require approval before external changes.

faq.question: Are scheduled checks and GitHub starring required?
faq.answer: No. Both are optional and require consent. Scheduled checks execute external packages, while GitHub starring also requires authenticated GitHub CLI access.
